---
title: "Room-mode model"
---

Workstream 2: the rectangular rigid-wall modal model of the room,
$L_x \times L_y \times L_z = 4.445 \times 3.658 \times 2.692\ \mathrm{m}$
(the [layout](layout.qmd) dimensions). Code in
[`scripts/room_modes.py`](https://github.com/madi-lts/roomANC/blob/master/scripts/room_modes.py),
which also regenerates every figure and table on this page.

## Model

With rigid walls the eigenfunctions and eigenfrequencies are

$$
\psi_{\mathbf{n}}(x,y,z) = \cos\frac{n_x \pi x}{L_x}
\cos\frac{n_y \pi y}{L_y} \cos\frac{n_z \pi z}{L_z},
\qquad
f_{\mathbf{n}} = \frac{c}{2}\sqrt{\left(\frac{n_x}{L_x}\right)^2 +
\left(\frac{n_y}{L_y}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{n_z}{L_z}\right)^2},
$$

where $\mathbf{n} = (n_x, n_y, n_z)$ are non-negative mode indices
(**axial** = one nonzero index, **tangential** = two, **oblique** = three)
and $c = 343\ \mathrm{m/s}$. The field at drive frequency $f$ is modeled as
the damped modal sum

$$
p(\mathbf{r}; f) \;=\; \sum_{\mathbf{n}} \frac{a_{\mathbf{n}}\,
\psi_{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{r})}{f_{\mathbf{n}}^2 - f^2 + i f \,\Delta f},
$$

with uniform modal half-power bandwidth
$\Delta f = 2.2/T_{60} \approx 5.5\ \mathrm{Hz}$ (for the assumed
$T_{60} \approx 0.4$ s) and equal modal excitation $a_{\mathbf{n}} = 1$.
The true $a_{\mathbf{n}}$ depend on the unknown, distributed
structure-borne source coupling, so absolute and inter-mode levels below
are indicative only; what is robust is the *geometry* — which modes
dominate near each tone and where their null surfaces sit. Rigid-wall
eigenfrequencies also run a few Hz high of reality (compliant walls lower
them); the level-vs-position map of the
[measurement plan](measurements.qmd#next-measurements) is the ground truth
that will pin both down.

This confirms the coincidence table in the [layout](layout.qmd): every
measured line lands within (or at the edge of) the $\pm\Delta f/2$ band of
at least one mode except the 46.9 Hz (0,1,0), which sits in a gap of the
source spectrum. The density is still low — between 30 and 85 Hz there are
only seven modes — which is the modal-control regime the
[physics argument](physics.qmd#modal-vs-diffuse-regime) relies on.

## Pressure field at the two fundamentals

![Modeled $|p|$ at 59.0 Hz: plan at pillow height $z = 0.65$ m and
elevation through the bed centerline $y = 2.66$ m. Dashed contour:
−20 dB re the in-slice maximum (the predicted null trench). Dots: error
mics; squares: subwoofer corners (filled = phase 1); dotted rectangle:
current bed; green star and dashed rectangle: the
[recommended head position and bed footprint](#recommended-bed-placement).](images/pressure-59hz.png){#fig-p59}

At 59.0 Hz the response is shared between **(1,1,0)**
($|f_{\mathbf{n}} - f| = 1.7$ Hz) and **(0,0,1)** (4.7 Hz), as the
coincidence analysis anticipated. Consequences:

- The null set is not the bare $x = L_x/2$, $y = L_y/2$ cross of (1,1,0):
  interference with (0,0,1) and the off-resonant background bends it into
  the curved trench visible in both slices, running near midroom and
  rising from $z \approx 1$ m toward the ceiling with increasing $x$.
- **The bed is off the trench but far from quiet.** The slice maximum is
  the S1 corner; the pillow zone ($y \gtrsim 2.7$ m, head wall) reads
  16–23 % of it (−13 to −16 dB) — 8–10 dB above the trench floor the
  model says is available (see
  [recommended placement](#recommended-bed-placement)).
- Every error mic sits well off the −20 dB trench at both tones, i.e. the
  perimeter array observes the dominant modes at good SNR.

![Modeled $|p|$ at 39.9 Hz, same slices and markings. The field is
essentially the (1,0,0) axial mode: a single null plane at
$x = L_x/2 = 2.22$ m, uniform in $z$.](images/pressure-40hz.png){#fig-p40}

## Recommended bed placement

Minimizing the modeled $|p|$ at head height $z = 0.65$ m, with 59 Hz
weighted 10:1 in power over 39.9 Hz (it dominates perceptually), puts the
**optimal head position at $(x, y) \approx (2.51, 1.31)$ m** (origin at
S1's corner): −24 dB re the slice maximum at 59 Hz and −14 dB at
39.9 Hz, against −13 to −16 dB and −9 dB at the current pillow
positions — a predicted passive gain of **8–10 dB at 59 Hz and
~5 dB at 39.9 Hz** for rotating the bed 180° with the head toward
midroom (footprint $x \approx 1.75$–$3.25$, $y \approx 1.3$–$3.3$ m, foot
at the current head wall; the green overlay in @fig-p59 and @fig-p40).
The minimum is not a knife-edge: ±20 cm in any direction stays below
−21 dB at 59 Hz.

The robust part of this is that $x \approx L_x/2 = 2.22$ m is a null of
every odd-$n_x$ mode at once — (1,0,0) under the 39.9 Hz tone and (1,1,0)
under the drone. What survives there at 59 Hz is mostly (0,0,1), whose
null plane $z = H/2 = 1.35$ m a bed cannot reach — which is why ANC
remains the primary tool. The exact $y$ and the shift from 2.22 to
$\approx 2.5$ m inherit the equal-excitation assumption, so the spot
should be confirmed against the measured level-vs-position map before
furniture moves; moving the bed also relocates M1/M2 and triggers
re-identification (spec R7).

At 39.9 Hz only **(1,0,0)** is within $\Delta f$; the next mode, (0,1,0)
at 46.9 Hz, is 7 Hz away and contributes the weak $y$-asymmetry in the
plan view. A single dominant controllable mode is the easiest possible
control problem — two corner subs driven differentially couple to it
directly ([layout](layout.qmd#subwoofers-start-with-2-diagonal-expand-to-4)).

## Observability of the 6-mic array

The promised numerical score of the layout's observability matrix
$\Psi_{mn} = \psi_{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{x}_m)$ ($m$ over the six mic
positions, $\mathbf{n}$ over the modes within $\pm\Delta f$ of each
controlled tone), by its singular values $\sigma$:

| Tone (Hz) | Modes within $\pm\Delta f$ | $\sigma_{\min}$ | $\sigma_{\max}$ | $\operatorname{cond}(\Psi)$ |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 39.9 | (1,0,0) | 1.60 | 1.60 | 1.0 |
| 59.0 | (1,1,0), (0,0,1) | 0.85 | 1.27 | 1.5 |
| 79.9 | (1,0,1), (2,0,0), (0,1,1) | 0.42 | 2.04 | 4.8 |
| 117.9 | (0,2,1), (3,0,0), (1,2,1), (2,2,0) | 0.32 | 2.26 | 7.1 |
| 120.0 | (3,0,0), (1,2,1), (2,2,0), (3,1,0) | 0.45 | 2.52 | 5.6 |

Every mode group is full rank with $\operatorname{cond}(\Psi) \le 7.1$
and $\sigma_{\min} \ge 0.32$ — no mode near any controlled tone is close
to unobserved, including the four-mode clusters at the 117.9/120.0 Hz
harmonics that motivated six mics over four
([layout](layout.qmd#error-microphones-a-6-mic-perimeter-array)). These
numbers use the M1/M2 positions adopted with
[virtual pillow sensing](layout.qmd#virtual-error-sensing-at-the-pillows)
(the relocation improves the 59 Hz pair: $\operatorname{cond}$ 2.3 → 1.5).
The layout stands; no further mic moves indicated.

## What this changes downstream

- The 59 Hz controller must manage **two** modes of opposite vertical
  character (§ pressure field). Height-diverse mics observe both, but the
  diagonal sub pair drives them only in a fixed ratio; setting them
  independently room-wide needs an adjacent pair or more corners
  ([layout](layout.qmd#subwoofers-start-with-2-diagonal-expand-to-4)).
- Predicted null trenches are where the verification grid
  ([spec](spec.qmd#measurement-and-verification-plan)) should sample most
  densely: residual-pattern failures show up there first.
- The level-vs-position map (next measurement) overlays directly on
  @fig-p59 / @fig-p40; a measured null displaced from the predicted one
  calibrates the effective wall compliance, which this rigid-wall model
  deliberately omits.
